references.text: The first servant received ten cities for his ten minas. Here in verse 19, the second servant receives five cities for his five minas—both are rewarded proportionally according to their faithfulness ([ref:Luk 19:17|Luke 19:17]).

In Jesus' parable of the talents in Matthew, servants are also rewarded based on how faithful they were with what was entrusted to them. The one who received two talents and earned two more received the same commendation as the one who earned five ([ref:Matt 25:21-23|Matthew 25:21-23]).
Paul emphasizes that each will receive their reward according to their own work, a principle reflected in the servant with five minas receiving five cities ([ref:1 Kor 3:8|1 Corinthians 3:8]).

Jesus teaches that whoever is faithful in little is also faithful in much. The servant showed faithfulness with five minas and was therefore entrusted with authority over five cities ([ref:Luk 16:10|Luke 16:10]).
In Revelation, the one who conquers and holds fast to Jesus' deeds is promised power over the nations—a parallel to the reward of ruling over cities ([ref:Åp 2:26|Revelation 2:26]).
Daniel prophesies that the holy ones will receive the kingdom—an eschatological parallel to faithful servants being given dominion over cities in God's kingdom ([ref:Dan 7:22|Daniel 7:22]).
Paul writes that if we endure, we will also reign with Christ. Being placed over cities illustrates this co-reigning with Christ ([ref:2 Tim 2:12|2 Timothy 2:12]).
